grammar.0.title: Relative clause: verb at the end, commas on both sides
grammar.0.text: A Relativsatz gives more information about the noun before it (“who”, “which”). The relative pronoun takes the gender of the noun it refers to (der/das/die). The verb goes at the end.
grammar.1.note: Gender and number = the noun before; case = its role in the relative clause. Nominativ: „der Handwerker, der repariert“; Akkusativ: „die Hilfe, die ich brauche“ (ich = subject, so die = object).
grammar.2.title: Examples of Relativsatz
grammar.2.note: First the main clause, then a comma, the relative clause, and a comma. The verb is at the end of the relative clause.
grammar.2.rows.0.1: That's the flat that I'm looking for.
grammar.2.rows.1.1: I know someone who is a craftsman.
grammar.2.rows.2.1: The caretaker whom I call is nice.
grammar.2.rows.3.1: I like the room that is bright.
quiz.8.why: Relativsatz: comma + verb at the end.
